analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md (head lines 3, 9-13) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (patch hunk @@ -1508, the engine_v2_max_concurrent row). The base text for the CLI reference was not supplied, only the patch, so the surrounding document was not examined.

Documented behavior change: on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra, models on the native `auto` paged allowlist now start at the unqualified legacy ceiling of 8 instead of 4 when the setting is automatic. Widths above 8 still require a reviewed profile. A width above the configured one returns to it under Low Power Mode or thermal pressure. Explicit operator values are preserved.

Security relevance: this is a scheduling-concurrency and availability change, touching T-010, T-029 and TB-007. It does not touch the encrypted prefix cache, so T-041 is unaffected: no TTL, HMAC, scope or gating changes appear. It does not touch attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or the coordinator WebSocket boundary (TB-002). The documented ceiling stays inside the existing legacy [1, 8] bound and the architecture and memory gates.

Possible interaction for a later source pass: a higher default concurrency could increase GPU or memory pressure and the number of simultaneous decrypted prompts held in process memory (A-001, T-014, T-028). The code implementing the default (BackendSettings, ServingPerformanceProfiles) is not in this batch, so the memory-reserve and thermal-fallback behavior is unverified. The documentation states that these changes do not lower reserves.

No findings. The threat model needs no update from the supplied evidence.
